RagShortTexts: The standing military of Greuthungians in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Greuthungians rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Greuthungians against overwhelming regional adversaries.

Horse archers form a loose screen ahead of the wagons, bows drawn and arrows ready. When the signal horn sounds, the screen wheels and feigns a retreat, drawing enemy riders into the marsh where the infantry waits. A missed signal costs lives, and every rider knows the command call by heart.

Over the steppe from a barrow, the field officers study the terrain. Victory depends on keeping the supply herds clear of the enemy column and holding the center until the heavy horsemen are released. Each chieftain's contingent is judged by how quickly it answers the signals, and the failures are counted in the next season's tribute.
